trust_decision.summary: Whether an API caller may start a binary update from an index URL they supply with the version (downgrade) check skipped. The endpoint's Write permission decides this in service/core/api.go, and authenticateRequest enforces it. PermitAnyone short-circuits all authentication.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the route /api/v1/updates/from-url, which is registered here with Write: api.PermitAnyone.

fix_sites.entry_point: Go method (*updates.Updater).UpdateFromURL, reached only from the endpoint above
fix_sites.module_kind: updater core library (dead code after endpoint removal)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered route was found to dismiss. The other ignoreVersion=true callers are local CLI tools (cmds/cmdbase/update.go:51, cmds/updatemgr/download.go:78), and a solver would rightly treat them as not network-exposed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: updates/check and updates/apply (PermitUser) and the CLI ForceUpdate path (ignoreVersion=true, forceApply=true) must keep working. A fix that hardens updateAndUpgrade itself, for example by always enforcing ShouldUpgradeTo or HTTPS-only URLs, would break the CLI update and updatemgr download tools.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Configure() accepts new index URLs at runtime without re-running the HTTPS check from Config.Check (module.go:136-141). A config-option-driven custom index URL route would be a how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Release-channel switching already flows through Configure (service/core/update_config.go:131-133). A maintainer could add a 'custom update server' option for support cases.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted 'updates/apply' variant (for example a support-channel switch or a reinstall endpoint) that calls updateAndUpgrade with ignoreVersion=true under a weaker permission.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The neighbouring update endpoints are registered inline with ad-hoc permissions. A support or downgrade action is a plausible feature. It is WHERE-type only.

O9_family: missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) on a local HTTP API endpoint that triggers a software update or downgrade

O10_build.toolchain: Go toolchain (go.mod at repo root); the Angular/Tauri desktop parts are not needed for this area
O10_build.project_tests: base/api/authentication_test.go (permission matrix); service/updates/updates_test.go (updateAndUpgrade with local data). There is no test for the from-url endpoint.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change Write: api.PermitAnyone to api.PermitUser/PermitAdmin on updates/from-url (this is effectively a correct fix; the published fix deletes the endpoint).

out_of_scope_notes: service/interop/api.go:16-25 registers interop/ping with Write: api.PermitAnyone; it is a different sink (interop ping handlers).
Commit 67b684c is only a version bump and npm/cargo lockfile update; it has no source changes for this advisory.

UpdateFromURL passes the caller URL without the HTTPS check that Config.Check applies to configured URLs (service/updates/module.go:136-141 vs 503). Index signature verification still applies via cfg.Verify (service/updates/downloader.go:85).
unverified: Database/config write API permissions (route to change core/releaseChannel) were not fully traced; assumed authenticated (base/api/database.go:42 sets dbCompatibilityPermission = PermitAdmin for the bridge).

single_site is not flagged because the fix touches two functions (endpoint registration plus the now-dead UpdateFromURL). In practice the protection sits at one route, and no O2 site or O8 route was found.
present_in_latest is not applicable (no O8 routes; latest release: none).
